primary_findings.why_it_matters:
Running `seed_e2e_data.py --reset` on a dev/test database deletes the `users` rows for alice/bob/carol/dan even when those rows were created by a real LDAP login, not by this script — the script creates them only when missing (`if existing is None:` at line 163) but deletes them unconditionally by derived id. Because `user_id` is `uuid5(NAMESPACE_DNS, username)`, the seed id and the real-account id are the same value, so a real account's `roles`, `status` and `token_version` (the revocation counter) are wiped, and any `user_projects` grant for those users in other projects is removed as well (`user_projects.user_id` is `ForeignKey("users.user_id", ondelete="CASCADE")`). Worst case: a DISABLED account is silently re-enabled — the login path rejects a disabled user only because the row says DISABLED (`if row is not None and is_disabled_status(row.status)`), and once the row is gone the next login recreates it with `status=UserStatus.ACTIVE.value`. This directly contradicts the script's own stated contract ("只删自己造的 —— `--reset` 按固定 UUID 列表筛，不碰业务数据") and the batch's must-not-regress rule 6.

脚本 docstring 把「--reset 只删自己造的」列为三条硬约束之一，理由写得很清楚：「不筛的话，在开发库里跑一次脚本 = 业务数据被删」。但 `_delete_own_rows` 一共删 5 类行（UserProject / Stream / Project / Workspace / User），这条用例只造了一条**外部 Workspace** 当「别人的数据」，其余 4 张表一个外部样本都没有 ⇒ 只要有人把 `delete(User).where(User.user_id.in_(user_ids))` 的过滤条件写漏成 `delete(User)`，这条用例照样绿，而开发库的用户行会被整表清空（`users` 里的角色/停用状态也一起没了）。
primary_findings.suggested_fix: Restrict the reset delete to rows this script actually created: tag seeded users with a seed-specific marker and filter `delete(User)` on that marker instead of the name-derived ids; if no marker is adopted, drop the `delete(User)` statement entirely (`_ensure_users` is already idempotent - it skips an existing row - so the user delete is not needed for idempotency) and preserve an existing row's `status`/`roles` instead of recreating the user with `status="ACTIVE"`. Extend `tests/scripts/test_seed_e2e_data.py::test_reset_only_deletes_our_own_rows` to be table-driven (a foreign row in User / Stream / Project / UserProject each) and assert the foreign user row survives a reset unchanged.

pcs-backend/app/core/ai_audit_middleware.py:175 -- the replay closure captures `body`, so the joined 10 MB copy stays resident for the whole downstream request
pcs-backend/app/main.py:245 --     app.add_middleware(AIAuditMiddleware)  # registered outside the router ⇒ outside the auth dependency `current_actor`

primary_findings.why_it_matters: The audit middleware sits outside routing and therefore outside authentication, so any anonymous client can make the server hold its body in RAM before a single credential is checked. Per in-flight request the memory cost is roughly **2× the body**: the accumulating `chunks` list (~10 MB at the cap) plus the `b"".join(chunks)` copy (~10 MB) at the moment of the join, after which the joined copy stays alive for the whole downstream call (the replay closure and the `_record_audit(..., body=body)` argument both keep a reference). The `_MAX_BODY_BYTES` cap is a *per-request* cap, not an aggregate one, so N concurrent max-size uploads cost ~10·N MB resident (~20·N MB transient at the join): on a 512 MB worker roughly 25 concurrent 10 MB uploads to `/api/v1/ai/*` exhaust the process, and on a 1 GB worker roughly 50 do. The cap is also 3–4 orders of magnitude above any legitimate payload: the AI request schemas (`app/schemas/ai.py`) are small JSON objects (a free-text `text`, a `query`, a few optional strings), so nothing legitimate ever approaches 10 MB. Buffering the body before the 501 stub does its work is the wrong trade: the same information is already available from `Content-Length`.
primary_findings.suggested_fix: In `pcs-backend/app/core/ai_audit_middleware.py`: (1) lower `_MAX_BODY_BYTES` from 10 MB to a size that matches the AI schemas — assume 256 KB is generous for a `text`/`query` payload and make it a settings-backed value so operators can raise it; (2) accumulate into a single `bytearray` (`buf.extend(chunk)`) and return `bytes(buf)` instead of a list + `b"".join(...)`, which removes the second full copy and halves peak memory; (3) before reading, inspect the `content-length` header and return 413 immediately when it exceeds the cap, so an oversized body is never buffered at all. Assumption: no legitimate AI request exceeds 256 KB — the schemas have no unbounded fields today, and `max_length` can be added to `AiIntentRequest.text` / `AiKnowledgeSearchRequest.query` in `app/schemas/ai.py` to make that guarantee explicit.

round-2 independent validation: 'the prefix test runs before routing, so an anonymous POST to /api/v1/ai/<anything> (even an unrouted path) has its body read at line 162 and hashed in the finally block'
pcs-backend/app/core/ai_audit_middleware.py:147-149 -- the prefix test runs BEFORE routing (no path boundary)
primary_findings.why_it_matters:
`_sanitize_text` runs five regexes over the *entire* request body, and the EMAIL rule is an unanchored `X+@…` pattern: the greedy `[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+` consumes the rest of the string, the following literal `@` never matches, and the engine then retries the tail once per consumed character **at every start offset** — i.e. O(n²) backtracking on a string that contains no `@`. The body is sanitized either as raw text (when JSON parsing fails) or per string value (when it succeeds), so a single request whose payload is a long run of `x`/`a` characters — inside `{"text": "…"}` or as a non-JSON body — drives the sanitizer into the quadratic regime. The audit hash is computed for every body up to 1 MB (`MAX_HASH_BYTES`), which is exactly the window where this bites: the existing tests sit just *outside* it (1 MB + 1024 and 10 MB + 1024 are both “too big to hash”). Because `_sanitize_text` is a plain synchronous call inside the async middleware, the cost lands on the single event-loop thread, so one such request stalls every other request handled by that worker — no `await` point is reached while the regex runs. The other four patterns are linear and unaffected.

⚠️ **round 2：已实测**（**级别维持 P1** —— 独立验证认为 P0 过高，见下）。hermes（GLM-5.2）在本机独立测得二次方，本机复核**走生产函数 `hash_sanitized`** 复现：40 KB ⇒ 1 107 ms，80 KB ⇒ 4 245 ms，160 KB ⇒ 17.0 s，320 KB ⇒ 68.1 s；对照组（body 含 `@`，走线性快路）80 KB ⇒ 1.5 ms。尺寸 ×2 ⇒ 时间 ×4，干净 O(n²)，且**全部落在 `MAX_HASH_BYTES = 1 MiB` 之内**。⇒ **一个未认证的 320 KB POST 到 `/api/v1/ai/*` 就能把事件循环钉住 68 秒**（80 KB ⇒ 4.2 s），期间**整个服务的所有端点一起卡住**：`_record_audit` 在中间件的 `finally` 里、**认证之前**执行，`hash_sanitized` 是同步 CPU 且无 await 点 ⇒ 不是「一个请求慢」，是**整站不可用**。⇒ 这不再是「perf regression」（P2 口径），而是**未认证的可用性缺陷** ⇒ P0。修复顺序应与 #3 同批（同一条请求路径 ⇒ 一次改动同治）。

⚠️ **round 2 独立验证的两处措辞更正（已采纳）**：(a) **不是「认证之前」** —— body 在中间件里于路由前就被读走（line 162），但**哈希发生在 `finally` 里、响应已发出之后**（line 202）；可利用性不变（审计行在每种结果下都会写），且 5 次/分的 RBAC 限流只改响应码、**不阻止哈希**。(b) **可达面比原报告写的更宽** —— 前缀判定发生在**路由之前** ⇒ **任何 `/api/v1/ai/<任意>`（包括未注册路由的路径）** 都会被读 body、哈希并入审计行。⇒ **级别维持 P1**（独立验证：影响仅限可用性、无数据丢失/无越权，CVSS AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H = 7.5；且同一条请求路径上的兄弟项 #3、#18 同为 P1），但仍是「**未认证 · 单请求 · 整站事件循环停摆**」，**排修复队列第一位**（与 #3 一次改动同治）。
primary_findings.suggested_fix: Bound the greedy quantifiers in the EMAIL rule so a single start offset can only do a constant amount of work, e.g. `re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]{1,64}@[A-Za-z0-9.-]{1,255}\.[A-Za-z]{2,24}")` — with bounded repeats the scan becomes linear in the body length instead of quadratic, and 64/255 are the RFC 5321 limits so no realistic address is lost. Independently, cap the number of characters `_sanitize_text` scans per string (truncate the scanned prefix, e.g. first 64 KB per string) so the audit hash cost is bounded regardless of pattern shape. Note: I could not execute a benchmark in this review environment (no shell), so the quadratic claim is derived from the pattern shape (unanchored search + greedy `+` followed by a literal that cannot match) rather than measured — the bounded-quantifier change is safe to apply either way.
primary_findings.round2_note: round 2 (hermes glm-5.2 + 本机复核 + 独立验证): 级别 P1 -> P0 **被独立验证否决**，维持 P1（仅可用性影响，CVSS 7.5；兄弟项 #3/#18 同路径同为 P1）。'not measured' caveat 已由实测数字取代；两处措辞更正已采纳（哈希发生在响应之后的 finally 里；可达面比原报告更宽 —— 任何 /api/v1/ai/<任意> 未注册路径同样被哈希）。

primary_findings.why_it_matters: Redis unreachable ⇒ enqueue raises ⇒ the exception is caught ⇒ False is returned ⇒ the middleware logs one warning line and the request proceeds to return 501 as usual. The audit table stops recording entirely for the duration of the outage — which is exactly the window in which probing or a misconfiguration is most likely — and nothing in the product surface reports it: `/api/v1/health/ai` exposes only endpoint/CIDR configuration, never the state of the audit pipeline. An operator sees a healthy AI status, an empty audit table, and no way to distinguish "no AI traffic" from "audit blind". The batch's own must-not-regress list requires that the audit table not be blind to probing behaviour, and this is the one path where it goes blind without a single failed request.

Assumption: a process-local counter is acceptable as a first cut; a DB heartbeat written by the worker is the stronger version and would also cover the "worker down" case.

primary_findings.why_it_matters:
If the insert fails — p10_001 not applied on the target database (UndefinedColumn on `request_id`), a transient DB error, a lock timeout — the task swallows the exception and returns normally. ARQ therefore records the job as *successful* and deletes it: no retry (the module's own docstring states arq 0.28 only retries on `Retry`), no dead-letter, and the row never appears in `ai_audit_log`. The AI request already returned 501, so the caller sees nothing wrong, and the audit table — whose entire purpose is to make AI probing visible — silently omits precisely the requests an attacker would want hidden. The worker configures `max_tries = 3`, but a swallowed exception never consumes a try, so that budget is unreachable for this task.

DO NOTHING`），重试不会产生重复行。改成有界重试既符合本仓既有模式，也不会带来重试风暴。

The only test of the new "real backend" channel asserts three things: the login button navigates home, a dashboard heading is visible, and no console error was emitted. primary_findings.why_it_matters: 中间件在 `finally` 块里 `await self._record_audit(...)`，而 `_record_audit` 会走到 `arq.create_pool` —— ARQ 0.28 的 `create_pool` 在连不上时会**重试 `conn_retries`（默认 5）次、每次间隔 `conn_retry_delay`（1 秒）、单次连接超时 `conn_timeout`（1 秒）**，最坏约 6×(1s 连接 + 1s 间隔) ≈ 10 秒。而 ASGI 应用在 `finally` 结束前不会返回 ⇒ uvicorn 无法回收/复用这条 HTTP 连接（响应字节虽已写出，但连接要等 10 秒才归还）。也就是说 Redis 一挂，**每一个 `/api/v1/ai/*` 请求都会把连接钉住约 10 秒**，吞吐被旁路审计拖垮；P10-B 接上真实 AI 端点后这条路径的 QPS 会比现在的 501 占位高一个量级。审计是旁路，本不该有能力占住业务请求的连接 —— 这里缺的是一个显式的超时/快速失败边界（bulkhead）。

primary_findings.title: Audit hash is computed outside the degrade guard: nested JSON kills the audit row and escapes the middleware
primary_findings.first_evidence: pcs-backend/app/core/ai_audit_middleware.py:202 --         digest = hash_sanitized(body) if len(body) <= MAX_HASH_BYTES else None
evidence: pcs-backend/app/core/ai_audit_middleware.py:202 -- digest = hash_sanitized(body) if len(body) <= MAX_HASH_BYTES else None
pcs-backend/app/core/ai_audit_middleware.py:203-206 -- try: / await enqueue_ai_audit_log(...) / except Exception:  # the digest line sits OUTSIDE this try, so a hashing failure is not degraded
pcs-backend/app/core/ai_sanitizer.py:122-125 -- parsed = json.loads(text) / except json.JSONDecodeError:  # RecursionError is NOT a JSONDecodeError => it escapes hash_sanitized

pcs-backend/app/core/ai_sanitizer.py:90-98 -- sanitize_for_ai recurses once per nesting level with no depth bound (dict/list comprehensions), so the same body also blows the recursion limit in the sanitizer
pcs-backend/app/core/ai_audit_middleware.py:176-188 -- finally: / await self._record_audit(...)  # an exception raised here escapes __call__ and replaces any in-flight exception
pcs-backend/app/core/ai_sanitizer.py:117-133 -- hash_sanitized is the only caller of json.loads/sanitize_for_ai in the audit path
primary_findings.why_it_matters: Every AI request that reaches the middleware is supposed to leave exactly one audit row. The digest is computed *before* the try/except that is supposed to degrade audit failures, and `hash_sanitized` can raise: it calls `json.loads` and only catches `json.JSONDecodeError`, so a body with deep nesting (a few KB of nested arrays/dicts, e.g. ~1000 levels) raises `RecursionError`, which is not a `JSONDecodeError`. That exception escapes `_record_audit` entirely, so (a) the row is never enqueued — the audit table stays blind to exactly the kind of hostile/garbage payload an auditor wants to see — and (b) the exception escapes the middleware's `finally` block, replacing whatever exception was in flight and turning a handled request into an unhandled ASGI error after the response was already sent. The fix is two-part because only guarding the call site is not enough: if the digest is simply computed inside the try, the enqueue is skipped and the row is still lost. The digest must degrade to `None` (row still written) and the hashing itself must survive unbounded nesting.
primary_findings.suggested_fix: Two coordinated edits. (1) In `app/core/ai_audit_middleware.py::_record_audit`, compute the digest defensively and always enqueue the row: `try: digest = hash_sanitized(body) if len(body) <= MAX_HASH_BYTES else None / except Exception: logger.warning('AI 审计哈希失败（哈希留空，行照写）', exc_info=True); digest = None` — then keep the existing try around `enqueue_ai_audit_log`. The row must survive even when the hash cannot be computed (contract: audit rows must not be silently dropped). (2) In `app/core/ai_sanitizer.py::hash_sanitized`, treat unbounded nesting as a normal input: catch `RecursionError` alongside `json.JSONDecodeError` (fall back to hashing the sanitized raw text) and add a `depth` argument to `sanitize_for_ai` with a bounded maximum (e.g. 20) beyond which the value is replaced by a placeholder such as `"[DEEP]"`. Add a regression test that POSTs a body of ~1000 nested arrays to `/api/v1/ai/intent` and asserts the audit enqueue still happened (and that the response is not a 5xx from an escaped exception).

primary_findings.why_it_matters: The audit middleware is pure ASGI and runs on the event loop; `hash_sanitized` is a plain synchronous function, so its whole cost is paid by the loop thread with no `await` in between. For a 1 MB body that is a `json.loads` (building a Python object graph several times larger than the payload), a recursive walk applying five regexes to every string, a canonical `json.dumps` re-serialization and a sha256 — tens of milliseconds of pure CPU per request, all of it head-of-line blocking for every other request that worker is concurrently serving. The cost is paid even though the AI endpoints are 501 stubs, i.e. the hash is the most expensive part of handling a request that does no work at all. This is also the code path the second finding's pathological input lands on.
primary_findings.suggested_fix: Move the hash off the event loop with `await asyncio.to_thread(hash_sanitized, body)` in `AIAuditMiddleware._record_audit` (`pcs-backend/app/core/ai_audit_middleware.py:202`), so the CPU work runs in the default threadpool instead of blocking the loop. primary_findings.why_it_matters: The SPEC's private-deployment rule (SPEC §2.5「私有化强制」) is enforced in exactly two places: the startup check in main.py's lifespan and the call-time re-check inside OutboundAIClient.call(). The startup check reads `ai_enabled` from system_settings once, at boot; when AI is off then, `validate_ai_startup_config` returns immediately without validating anything. The switch is a database row an administrator can flip at runtime through the parameters page, with no restart. And the call-time check is currently unreachable, because the five AI endpoints raise AINotImplementedError directly and never construct OutboundAIClient. So the sequence "admin enables ai_enabled and points ai_endpoint at a public URL" is blocked nowhere: the startup guard already ran, the request path never re-validates, and /health/ai merely reports degraded. Nothing calls a model today so there is no leak yet, but the invariant this batch was built to enforce is enforced by nothing at the moment it starts to matter, and the P10-B implementer inherits a guard that only fires once at boot.
primary_findings.suggested_fix: Move the check onto the request path: add a FastAPI dependency to the AI router that re-reads `ai_enabled` / `ai_endpoint` from system_settings on every AI request and calls `validate_ai_endpoint(endpoint, parse_cidrs(settings.internal_cidrs))`, rejecting with 503 when AI is enabled but the endpoint resolves outside the internal CIDRs. That way a runtime flip is validated by the same code path that serves the request, and P10-B cannot wire a route that skips it. Assumption: per-request re-validation is acceptable overhead for the five reserved endpoints.

primary_findings.title: Every AI request opens and tears down a fresh ARQ/Redis connection pool on the request path
evidence: pcs-backend/app/services/ai/arq_queue.py:64 --         pool = await _create_pool()
pcs-backend/app/services/ai/arq_queue.py:34 --     return await create_pool(RedisSettings.from_dsn(get_settings().redis_url))

pcs-backend/app/core/ai_audit_middleware.py:204 --             await enqueue_ai_audit_log(
pcs-backend/app/main.py:188 -- async def _close_redis_connections() -> None:  # the repo's existing process-level Redis-connection teardown hook
primary_findings.why_it_matters: `enqueue_ai_audit_log` builds a brand-new ARQ pool (TCP connect + AUTH against Redis) for every single audited request and closes it again in the `finally` block, so request N leaves behind N Redis connections' worth of handshake churn instead of reusing one pooled connection. The middleware calls this on every request to `/api/v1/ai/*` — including the 501 probes and the unauthorized probes — and it is awaited inside the request's `finally`, so the ASGI task (and with it the HTTP connection, for keep-alive clients) is not released until the Redis round-trip completes, even though the client has already received its response. The same create/close-per-call shape exists in `app/services/report/arq_queue.py`, but that path fires once per user-initiated long-running report job; here it is per request, on a path that is intended to become the hot AI path. The repo already has the process-level pattern this should follow: `app/services/broadcaster.py` and the WS registry keep a long-lived Redis connection and close it from the lifespan shutdown hook (`_close_redis_connections` in `app/main.py`).

Keep the per-call fallback path so that a Redis outage at first use degrades to the current warning-and-return-False behaviour instead of raising at import/startup time.

pcs-frontend/src/vite-env.d.ts:3 -- interface ImportMetaEnv {
pcs-frontend/src/vite-env.d.ts:4 --   readonly VITE_PROJECT_ID?: string;
pcs-frontend/playwright.config.ts:70 --       command: `VITE_ENABLE_MOCK=false npm run dev -- --port ${REAL_PORT}`,
primary_findings.why_it_matters: `src/vite-env.d.ts` augments `ImportMetaEnv` with only `VITE_PROJECT_ID` and `VITE_DEV_TOKEN`; Vite's own `ImportMetaEnv` carries a `[key: string]: any` index signature, so `import.meta.env.VITE_ENABLE_MOCK` is typed `any`. The real-backend E2E channel is selected by nothing but that comparison, so a wrong literal (`'FALSE'`, `'0'`, `'no'`) type-checks cleanly and silently leaves MSW mounted on port 5174 - the "真后端" suite then reports green without ever reaching the backend, which is the exact false-green this diff set out to eliminate. The `any` also removes the signal that this switch is a two-valued string rather than a boolean.
primary_findings.suggested_fix: Declare the variable in `src/vite-env.d.ts` as `readonly VITE_ENABLE_MOCK?: 'true' | 'false';` so the explicit member type takes precedence over the index signature and the comparison in `src/main.tsx` is type-checked against the two legal values (a mistyped literal becomes a compile error). Keep the runtime semantics unchanged ("mock on unless explicitly 'false'").

primary_findings.title: AI request bodies mix camelCase and snake_case within the same endpoint
primary_findings.first_evidence: pcs-backend/app/schemas/ai.py:68 --     equipment_tag: str | None = Field(None, description="已知设备位号")
evidence: pcs-backend/docs/openapi.json:21631 --           "projectId": {
pcs-backend/docs/openapi.json:21704 --           "equipment_tag": {
pcs-backend/app/schemas/ai.py:68 --     equipment_tag: str | None = Field(None, description="已知设备位号")
pcs-backend/app/schemas/ai.py:86 --     document_ref: str | None = Field(None, description="文档引用（规范号 / 文件 id）")
primary_findings.why_it_matters: The AI request family uses two conventions side by side: the fields SPEC defines are camelCase (`context.projectId`, `context.recordId`, `topK`), while the two bodies this repo defined on its own (D17) are snake_case (`equipment_tag`, `document_ref`). A single request body therefore mixes both -- `/api/v1/ai/equipment/recommend` takes `{equipment_tag, context: {projectId}}` -- so a frontend caller has to remember which convention applies per field rather than per API. The camelCase half is frozen by SPEC (D12 keeps `topK` verbatim), but the snake_case half was a free choice this batch made, so the inconsistency is avoidable: giving `equipment_tag` / `document_ref` the same camelCase aliases the SPEC fields use (with `populate_by_name=True`, so both spellings still enter) makes the whole AI request family read one way and leaves the server's internal snake_case names untouched.
primary_findings.suggested_fix: Give the two repo-defined AI request fields the same camelCase aliases the SPEC-defined ones use: in `pcs-backend/app/schemas/ai.py`, change `equipment_tag: str | None = Field(None, description="已知设备位号")` to `equipment_tag: str | None = Field(None, alias="equipmentTag", description="已知设备位号")` and likewise `document_ref` -> `alias="documentRef"` (the models already set `populate_by_name=True`, so `equipment_tag` continues to be accepted). Then regenerate `docs/openapi.json`, `openapi.snapshot.json` and `src/types/api.d.ts`, and extend `tests/api/v1/test_ai_routes.py` with an alias-acceptance assertion for the two new aliases (the pattern already exists for `topK`).

evidence: pcs-backend/docs/openapi.json:21800 --           "query"
pcs-backend/docs/openapi.json:21795 --             "default": 5

primary_findings.why_it_matters: The OpenAPI marks `AiKnowledgeSearchRequest.required` as `["query"]` only -- `topK` carries `"default": 5` and is optional -- and the server agrees (`top_k: int = Field(5, ...)`). But the generated TypeScript emits `topK: number;` with no `?`, so a TypeScript caller of `/api/v1/ai/knowledge/search` is forced by the type checker to send `topK` even though the contract says it may be omitted. pre_existing_findings.first_evidence: pcs-backend/scripts/check_migration_idempotency.py:112-115 -- func = node.func / if not isinstance(func, ast.Attribute) or not isinstance(func.value, ast.Name): / continue / op_name = f"op.{func.attr}"      ⇒ only `op.<method>` with a bare `op` receiver is inspected
evidence: pcs-backend/scripts/check_migration_idempotency.py:112-115 -- func = node.func / if not isinstance(func, ast.Attribute) or not isinstance(func.value, ast.Name): / continue / op_name = f"op.{func.attr}"      ⇒ only `op.<method>` with a bare `op` receiver is inspected

pcs-backend/scripts/check_migration_idempotency.py:173-178 -- paths = sorted({p for g in GLOBS for p in MIGRATIONS_DIR.glob(g)}) … if not violations: print(f"OK: 0 violations in {len(paths)} migrations ({' '.join(GLOBS)})")      ⇒ a skipped file is invisible in the report

pcs-backend/tests/scripts/test_check_migration_idempotency.py:64-83 -- test_check_detects_missing_if_not_exists writes a file using the canonical `op.create_index(` spelling      ⇒ the negative control never exercises an aliased receiver
pre_existing_findings.why_it_matters: The migration-idempotency ratchet detects `op.create_index(...)` only when the call's receiver is a bare Name called `op`. A migration written as `alembic.op.create_index("ix_x", "t", ["c"])` (import alembic) or with an aliased import (`from alembic import op as o`) yields a receiver that is an Attribute or a different Name, so the call is skipped entirely — the missing `if_not_exists=True` guard is never reported and the script still prints "OK: 0 violations in N migrations". That is the classic green-while-red shape this repository has already been bitten by twice (the docstring itself records the earlier "84 条漂移低估" incident caused by guessing structure from strings). The batch's new p10_001 migration is checked correctly for the canonical spelling, and the new-prefix coverage added in this diff (GLOBS plus `test_covered_globs_include_every_migration_prefix`) does correctly red-light a future `p11_*` prefix, so the remaining hole is the receiver-name dependency. This defect sits in unchanged code of the ratchet that this diff extended, so it is reported as pre-existing.
pre_existing_findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the receiver by alias instead of by literal name: per file, collect the module-level names bound to alembic's operations object (`op`, `alembic.op`, `operations`, any `as` alias) and treat calls on those receivers as op calls; additionally flag an `op.<method>`-shaped call whose receiver is not a recognised alias so the aliasing cannot silently disable the check. Add a negative-control test that writes a migration using `alembic.op.create_index(...)` and asserts it is reported.
pre_existing_findings.note: pre-existing: the batch edited scripts/check_migration_idempotency.py (it widened GLOBS to p10_* and tightened LEGACY_PREFIXES) but did not touch the op-receiver resolution, and the new migration p10_001 uses a bare `op.` receiver so it is covered. Nearby cleanup stays pre-existing.

residual_risks: Sanitizer rule order: the EMAIL rule is applied AFTER the LINE_NO / EQUIPMENT_TAG / PROJECT_NO rules. Those rules replace their match with a bracketed placeholder (e.g. 'AB-123' -> '[LINE_NO]'), and the EMAIL pattern's local-part class `[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+` does not include '[' or ']' — so an address whose local part contains a tag-shaped token (e.g. 'AB-123@corp.com') or a project-number-shaped token ('2024.001.001@corp.com') is NOT redacted; the address (and its domain) survives into the payload that would be sent to the model. Narrow trigger, but the ordering is the same class of trap the module docstring already documents for LINE_NO vs EQUIPMENT_TAG; moving EMAIL to the front of SENSITIVE_PATTERNS would close it.

Seed script `--reset` deletes the whole seed `Project` row but only clears `user_projects` and `streams` first. Any other row that references the project (equipment, records, `document_chunks`, `project_input_checklist`, ...) blocks the delete with an FK violation; the script does not catch it, so the reset aborts with a traceback instead of a clear message. This becomes reachable as soon as P10-B creates business rows under the E2E project.

Unauthenticated AI probes are subject to the pre-existing global RBAC rate limiter (>5 denied requests per minute per IP -> 429). A burst of invalid-token probes therefore returns 429 rather than 401, and the audit rows for those probes record status_code=429, not 401 — worth knowing when reading the audit table to investigate probing activity.

Audit amplification (by design, worth a rate-limit decision): every request whose path starts with /api/v1/ai produces one ARQ job plus one `ai_audit_log` row — including unauthenticated probes (contract 2 demands auth failures be recorded) and CORS preflights, since `AIAuditMiddleware` is registered outside `CORSMiddleware` and therefore sees preflight OPTIONS requests. An anonymous client can therefore grow both the Redis queue and the audit table without holding any credential. This follows from an explicit requirement, so it is a residual risk rather than a defect.

SSRF gate is sound today but time-of-check-to-time-of-use: `app/core/ai_cidr.py:130` resolves the endpoint hostname at call time, while a future HTTP client would resolve it again at connect time, so a hostname that answers with an internal IP during validation and a public IP at connect would pass the gate. Not exploitable in P10 (`OutboundAIClient.call` raises `AINotImplementedError` before any request is made), but the gate must be re-checked or the resolved IP pinned when the real call is implemented. Parsing itself was checked and is fail-closed: `host_of` uses `urlparse(...).hostname` (userinfo stripped, IPv6 literals handled), literal IPs skip DNS, address-family mismatches are skipped rather than raising, and any resolved IP outside the CIDRs causes rejection.

Unsanitized client-controlled text in the audit trail: `app/core/ai_audit_middleware.py:207` stores the request path verbatim (`endpoint=str(scope.get("path", ""))`, truncated to 200 chars by the writer) with no sanitization. Uvicorn percent-decodes the path, so an anonymous client can place arbitrary text — including `%0A` newlines — into the `endpoint` column of the audit table. Bounded to 200 characters and never used in a query, but it is unsanitized attacker-controlled text inside an audit table, and the sanitizer is not applied to it.

Token-type divergence between the audit middleware and the app: the middleware derives the audit `user_id` via `decode_token` directly (`app/core/ai_audit_middleware.py:73`) and therefore accepts a refresh token, while the application's own `_decode_bearer` rejects any token whose `type` is not `access` (`app/api/v1/auth.py:143`). The resulting audit row (401) is still attributed to the refresh token's legitimate owner, so this is not a forged attribution, but the two layers disagree on what a bearer token is. Forged/garbage tokens cannot produce a false attribution: `decode_token` verifies the HS256 signature (`app/core/security.py:135`), so an invalid token raises and the middleware records `user_id=None`.

The internal-only AI gate is currently unreachable from the request path: the five AI routes raise `AINotImplementedError` directly and never construct `OutboundAIClient`, so the CIDR validation in `outbound_ai_client.call` never runs in production traffic — the gate is defense-in-depth for a later batch. `ai_endpoint` is admin-writable only (`require_roles(actor, "SYSTEM_ADMIN")` in `app/api/v1/system_settings.py:52`), so a normal user cannot steer it.

Seed UUIDs are publicly derivable: `SEED_PROJECT_ID`, the workspace id and the four user ids are `uuid5(NAMESPACE_DNS, <well-known string>)` and therefore computable from the source tree. No credential is embedded and every seeded route still requires an authenticated, authorized user, so this does not grant access on its own; it only matters where mock login is enabled, which is already a dev-only opt-in gated by `PCS_ENABLE_MOCK_LOGIN` plus a production start-up assertion.

The AI audit middleware sits outside CORS in the built stack (Starlette's add_middleware inserts at position 0, so the last-added middleware is outermost: trace_id → AIAudit → CORS → router). A cross-origin deployment therefore records CORS preflight OPTIONS requests to /api/v1/ai/* as status_code=200 rows with response_summary="HTTP_200" — rows that read as successful AI requests in an audit trail. Same-origin (vite-proxy) deployments are unaffected. Not raised as a finding because the trigger (cross-origin deployment) could not be confirmed from the repository.

enqueue_ai_audit_log opens and closes an ARQ Redis pool per AI request, and a failing aclose() is swallowed with a warning. A persistent close failure could leak connections until Redis maxclients is exhausted — which would then silently disable auditing via the same chain as the Redis-down finding. Anchor 50: the leak path is plausible but not confirmed.

The migration ratchet is safe against a new prefix (GLOBS plus test_covered_globs_include_every_migration_prefix red-lights any uncovered file), but LEGACY_PREFIXES still swallows any future migration literally named `p1_…` or `p3s_…`: a developer following the old batch naming would be silently excluded from the guard.

The 422 branch declared for the five AI endpoints points at FastAPI's `HTTPValidationError` (`{detail: [{loc,msg,type}]}`), but the repo's global `RequestValidationError` handler actually renders the unified `ErrorResponse` envelope (`{code, message, detail, trace_id}`) -- see `pcs-backend/app/core/errors.py:278-290`. `ErrorResponse` is not a component schema at all (`grep` over `docs/openapi.json`: zero occurrences of a `"ErrorResponse"` schema key), so no endpoint's contract can name the body the server actually sends. This is repo-wide and pre-existing (every endpoint inherits it), so it is not attributed to this diff, but it does mean the AI contract's 'bad parameters' branch does not describe the real body -- relevant to the batch's must-not-regress rule 3 ('wrong parameters => 422, not 501'), which constrains the status code, not the body shape.

The `X-Request-ID` header the AI audit middleware sets is not written into the audit row's own identifier field; the row's idempotency key is the server-generated `request_id` (a body field, present only on the 501). triage_groups.title: Seed script: destructive reset scope and the get-or-create shape
triage_groups.context: scripts/seed_e2e_data.py is the one-shot E2E data source; its two remaining hazards are the reset delete set (#1) and the lock-free insert shape (#9).
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Fix #1 first (restrict the reset delete to rows the script itself created and keep a disabled foreign account disabled), then #9 (adopt the savepoint + re-read-the-winner get-or-create shape in the five helpers). #1's regression test is the table-driven reset test #1 asks for, which also closes the coverage gap for #9.
triage_groups.why: Both live in the same file and the same fix session; #1 is a P1 data-loss hazard and #9 is the concurrency variant of the same helper code.

triage_groups.title: AI audit middleware: body size, sanitizer cost and hashing on the request path
triage_groups.context: AIAuditMiddleware reads the body before authentication, hashes it on the event loop, and sanitizes it with an unbounded regex - all on the unauthenticated path.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Cap the body first (#3: reject on content-length, lower the cap to a settings-backed value, buffer into one bytearray), then bound the EMAIL quantifiers (#4), then move the hash behind a degrade guard and off the loop (#17 + #18, one edit: `await asyncio.to_thread(...)` inside the try).
triage_groups.why: They are one request path with one cost model; the size cap also shrinks what #4 and #18 have to chew on.

triage_groups.title: AI audit delivery: Redis outage, ARQ retries and the unmigrated database
triage_groups.context: The audit row is produced by an ARQ job behind a Redis queue; every failure point on that path currently degrades to silence.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Decide the delivery guarantee once, then fix in order: #6 (bounded `Retry`, matching report_tasks), #21 (distinguish a missing-migration schema error and give the worker a migrate dependency in compose), #5 (expose an audit-pipeline health signal), #16 (bound the enqueue with a timeout and conn_retries=0), #20 (reuse one pool), #24 (correct the stale ARQ premise in the test docstring).
triage_groups.why: One subsystem, one decision (how strong the audit guarantee is); #6's retry also makes #21 and #5 visible instead of silent.

triage_groups.title: Guards that cannot fail: architecture guard, partial-index predicate, PG cleanup
triage_groups.context: The batch's own verification mechanisms (architecture guard, migration-shape guard, PG lane cleanup) are all structurally unable to report a violation today.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Fix #7 first (it guards the batch's only-egress rule and currently passes on the natural bypass), then #10 (derive the partial-index predicate from the ORM index object and assert it in both guards), then #11 (assert the DROP SCHEMA returncode after the try/finally).
triage_groups.why: Each is a false-green in a different file but the same class: an assertion that cannot fail.

triage_groups.title: The real-backend E2E channel proves nothing about the seeded backend
triage_groups.context: The channel this batch built to catch mock drift can pass while the backend under test is not the database the seed wrote to, and while MSW is still mounted.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Fix #8 (align the backend DATABASE_URL with the seeded pcs_pgtest and assert a seeded row is visible), then #22 (an execution-level compose guard that runs migrate+seed and queries the result), then #23 (type the mock-toggle env var so a wrong literal cannot silently keep MSW on).
triage_groups.why: The three are the same false green seen from three angles: the wrong database, an unexecuted stack, and an untyped switch.

triage_groups.title: The published AI contract does not describe the reserved-endpoint contract
triage_groups.context: The five AI endpoints are contractually 501-only and auth-first, but the generated OpenAPI and the generated frontend types do not say so.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Fix #12 and #13 in one edit to the shared `responses` dict in app/api/v1/ai/routes.py, then regenerate openapi.json / openapi.snapshot.json / api.d.ts; decide the field-naming convention once for #26 (camelCase aliases for equipmentTag / documentRef) and once for #27 (whether topK stays optional with a server-side default) before changing the schema.
triage_groups.why: #12 and #13 are mechanical; #26 and #27 change the published request shape, so they need a decision first.

triage_groups.title: /health/ai: a malformed endpoint and an oversized handler
triage_groups.context: The new health endpoint answers 500 instead of `degraded` for a malformed admin-set endpoint, and its handler is ~97 lines against the repo's 50-line limit.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Fix #15 first (move the host extraction inside the degrade path and add an `endpoint_invalid` reason), then #14 (extract a pure `_classify_ai_endpoint` helper) - the refactor is easier once the try/except shape is settled.
triage_groups.why: Same function, and the refactor should not be done against a shape that is about to change.
